Architecting Local-First AI Systems (Part 2): Checkpointing, Persistence & Workflow Recovery

In Part 1, I shared how I'm building a pluggable multi-agent orchestration engine using LangGraph.
The next challenge wasn't AI—it was reliability.

What happens if a repository review takes several minutes and your laptop restarts?
What if an LLM call fails halfway through execution?
What if you want to resume an execution without starting over?
For production-grade AI systems, reliability is just as important as orchestration.
Key Architectural Decisions

Local-First Persistence
The platform runs entirely on a developer's laptop, so execution history, workflow state, checkpoints, and reports are stored locally using SQLite.

Serializing Complex State
Structured workflow state—including repository metadata, findings, metrics, and audit history—is serialized to JSON and reconstructed when the workflow resumes.

Checkpointing for Recovery
The orchestrator periodically saves execution checkpoints. If execution is interrupted, it resumes from the latest successful checkpoint instead of starting over.

Safe Background Execution
Long-running workflows execute asynchronously. Active task tracking ensures background tasks complete without being garbage collected.

Execution Flow
Workflow Request
│
▼
Start Background Task
│
▼
Execute LangGraph Nodes
│
▼
Save Checkpoint to SQLite
│
┌──────────┴──────────┐
│                     │
▼                     ▼
Continue Workflow      Failure
│                     │
▼                     ▼
Generate Report      Resume from Checkpoint

Why Local-First?
Source code never leaves your machine.
Works completely offline.
No cloud infrastructure.
Zero database hosting cost.
Simple setup.
Ideal for privacy-focused development.

The goal isn't just to build AI workflows—it's to build AI systems that are reliable, reproducible, and easy to run.

The project is open source. Contributions and feedback are welcome.
